vo.text: Tipped in! Anunoby tips it in!
Game 4 of the Finals. The Spurs led by as many as 29 at Madison Square Garden, and lost by one.

chunks.text: The Spurs led by as many as

vo.text: In all the years of the Finals, no team had ever blown a lead that big. The Spurs now own that record.

chunks.text: The Spurs now own that record

vo.text: Afterward, everyone said bad shots, mental collapse. Not wrong. But I went through the tracking data, and it's not that simple.
Start with the first half. Just how hot were the Spurs?

chunks.text: Just how hot were the Spurs?

vo.text: 41 to 22 after one. 14 threes in the half, the most in Finals history. Everything was falling.
But look closely, and a lot of these shots weren't easy.
Tracking data puts a make probability on every shot. At normal rates, the Spurs should have scored about 49 in the first half. Instead? They scored 70.
That extra 21 points was a hot hand. And a hot hand comes and goes. You can't ride it for a whole game.

chunks.text: And a hot hand comes and goes

vo.text: So where did the lead start to slip?
9:27 left in the third, Spurs up 29. Wembanyama swings an elbow into Towns' jaw. Flagrant 1.
And here's the thing: he already had 3 flagrant points this postseason. One more, and he's suspended. In the Finals. So how freely can he play now?

chunks.text: So how freely can he play now?

vo.text: From those two free throws, the Knicks ripped off a 13-0 run.
Look at this trip. The Spurs get four guys back, each on a man, and the whole lane, from the free-throw line to the rim, is empty.

chunks.text: The Spurs get four guys back

vo.text: By the time Wembanyama gets there, Anunoby's already thrown it down!
The Spurs shot 12 threes that quarter and made two. Every miss turned into a Knicks run-out. By the end of the quarter, the lead was down to 15.

chunks.text: By the end of the quarter

vo.text: Barkley wasn't wrong. With a lead that big, why keep jacking threes? Where's the logic in that?
So in the fourth, skip the threes and attack the rim. The Spurs did exactly that. The result? 4 for 19.
Why? Because the Knicks were right in their faces. On Spurs shots, the nearest defender's hand averaged just 2.7 feet from the ball. Less than an arm's length. How do you shoot over that?

chunks.text: How do you shoot over that?

vo.text: 9:30 left, Spurs up 20. Five minutes later, it was down to 4.
So run the numbers. The 21 bonus points from the first half? In the second half, they gave almost all of it back.
Still, with three and a half minutes left, the Spurs were up 7. How do you lose that?
3:31 left. Wembanyama hits a jumper. 104-97.
Believe it or not, that's the Spurs' last field goal of the game.
Two and a half minutes left. The Knicks get Wembanyama switched onto Brunson.

chunks.text: Two and a half minutes left

vo.text: Brunson doesn't care. 27 feet. Up it goes!
Then Wemby misses both free throws.
Brunson floater. Knicks in front.
Castle hits both free throws. Spurs back on top, 106-105.
And then, this play. Let's freeze it right here.
Up one, 13 seconds left, Spurs ball. And the shot clock reads more than the time left in the game.
So how do you play it? Simple. Do nothing. Hold the ball, and wait for them to foul you and send you to the line.

chunks.text: So how do you play it? Simple
and wait for them to foul you
and send you to the line

vo.text: And Fox? He gets the ball, never breaks stride, and goes straight at the rim.

chunks.text: and goes straight at the rim

vo.text: Pinned on the glass!
Now look at the clock. From the catch to takeoff, less than a second. Does that look like running out the clock?
That one play handed the Knicks a free possession. A whole night's work, gone.
5.7 seconds left. Brunson fires from 31 feet. Off the iron.
Everyone's watching him. Nobody picks up Anunoby crashing in.
Tipped in!
All game long, the Knicks led for just 53.8 seconds.
So here's the deal. The Spurs didn't just lose to bad shots. A big chunk of that 29-point lead was borrowed, and they paid it back in the second half.
What really gave it away were the possessions they threw away in the final three and a half minutes.
Three days later, the Spurs lost Game 5, and the Knicks won their first title since 1973.
